The discovery will have a momentous effect on the treatment of cancer.

definitions.text: (usually with "down") To write quickly.

examples.text: Just jot your name down on a piece of paper.
She carries a notebook so that she can jot down any ideas.

definitions.text: Anticipating something with anxiety or fear.
Perceptive; quick to learn; capable of understanding using one's intellect.

examples.text: They are apprehensive that some further disaster might occur.
She was apprehensive about receiving criticism of her performance.

definitions.text: The highest point.
A tall, sharp and craggy rock or mountain.

examples.text: Is man really the pinnacle of Creation, or just a freak of nature?
The pinnacle of evolution is the dolphin.

definitions.text: To deprive of nerve, force, or strength; to weaken; to enfeeble.
To make somebody nervous, upset, alarm, shake the resolve of.

examples.text: The company is running so well, it's unnerving.
Isn't it a bit unnerving that doctors call what they do 'practice'?

definitions.text: Domination, influence, or authority over another, especially by one political group over a society or by one nation over others.

examples.text: The whole world is denouncing US hegemony in world politics.
The US is doing everything to maintain its declining global hegemony.

definitions.text: A place where wine is made, or a company that makes wine.

examples.text: The winery offers tours with Adriano as the guide.
Governor Gavin Newsom ordered the closure of all bars and wineries in California.

definitions.text: Not prepared; caught by surprise.
A black mark given to a pupil who arrives at a lesson without the necessary items or preparation.

examples.text: I'm somewhat embarrassed that you've caught me so unprepared.
Never again will we face this unprepared.

definitions.text: Repellently frightful and shocking; horrific or ghastly.

examples.text: You shouldn't make fun of a subject as gruesome as death.
I saved him from a gruesome and humiliating death.

definitions.text: A small coin formerly circulated in England, rated at about a third of a farthing.
A lepton, a small coin used in Palestine in the time of Christ.

examples.text: Spider mites are a pest that damages English ivy.
Is there any home remedy for dust mites?

definitions.text: Of or pertaining to piety, exhibiting piety, devout, godfearing.

examples.text: Once upon a time there was a poor, pious girl.
I wish these pious people had reached more sensible conclusions.

definitions.text: Evasive and shifty

examples.text: The used car salesman seemed a bit dodgy to me.
That website seems a bit dodgy, I wouldn't enter your credit card information there.

definitions.text: A portable electronic device for recording images and audio on to a storage device, hence functioning as a camera and a recorder in a single unit

examples.text: My camcorder came with a video editor included.
Did your parents have a camcorder?

definitions.text: One who works in or with lead.
One who furnishes, fits, and repairs pipes and other apparatus for the conveyance of water, gas, or drainage.

examples.text: The plumber used many different tools to fix our sink.
Can you fix this or should I call a plumber?

definitions.text: To represent falsely; to inaccurately portray something.

examples.text: Journalists need to be careful not to misrepresent information.
He often misrepresents facts for his advantage.

definitions.text: A horizontal layer of igneous rock between older rock beds.
A piece of timber across the bottom of a canal lock for the gates to shut against.

examples.text: I wiped the window sill with a paper towel.
What is the name of that geranium on the window sill?

definitions.text: A reduction of some sort in an existing program.
Maneuver where the surfer turns and surfs back towards where the wave is breaking.

examples.text: Many employees had to be laid off due to budget cutbacks.
I was laid off from my job due to budget cutbacks.

definitions.text: Having cohesion.

examples.text: A text could be coherent but not cohesive, and vice versa.
None of those thoughts are cohesive nor do they make sense independently.

definitions.text: To pull back, especially in disgust, horror or astonishment.
To retreat before an opponent.
A starting or falling back; a rebound; a shrinking.

examples.text: The recoil reduces the weapon's accuracy.
This is a great rifle to snipe with, if you can handle the recoil.

definitions.text: One of the aristocracy, nobility, or people of rank in a community; one of a ruling class; a noble (originally in Revolutionary France).
A proponent of aristocracy; an advocate of aristocratic government.

examples.text: The aristocrat clings to the glory of his past.
In a good democracy, everyone should be an aristocrat.

definitions.text: A brahmin who acts as the hereditary superintendent of a particular ghat or temple, and is regarded as knowledgeable in matters of genealogy and ritual.
The red panda (Ailurus fulgens), a small raccoon-like animal of northeast Asia with reddish fur and a long, ringed tail.

examples.text: I'd never seen a panda until I went to China.
I had never seen a panda till that time.

definitions.text: Consciously thoughtful and observant (often of other people); caring
Characterised by careful and conscious thought; deliberate
To think about seriously.

examples.text: One should be considerate about things and considerate of people.
It was very considerate of you to buy that for Tom.

definitions.text: An individual who collects money from the public for some charitable cause.

examples.text: We're having a fundraiser to raise money for victims of Godzilla.
They all helped out at the charity fundraiser.

definitions.text: Not similar; unalike; different

examples.text: My preferences are very dissimilar to yours.
She felt that we were too dissimilar.

definitions.text: To contract; to draw together; to cause to shrink or wrinkle; to distort.
To shrink, cower, tense or recoil, as in fear, disgust or embarrassment.

examples.text: Why don't you calm down? You're really making me cringe.
I may be cringe, but you're mean, and that's worse.

definitions.text: To remove most of a tree, bush, or other rooted plant by cutting it close to the ground.
To remove a plant by pulling it out by the roots.
Something blunted, stunted, or cut short, such as stubble or a stump.

examples.text: The only article I could find on Wikipedia was just a stub.
On a pay stub are mentioned: the gross salary and the net salary.

definitions.text: In a solemn manner.

examples.text: The soldiers solemnly draped the flag over the coffin.
The poet wanted to solemnly celebrate life's beauty with their works.

definitions.text: Apathetic with regard to an apparent need or problem.
Uncritically satisfied with oneself or one's achievements; smug.

examples.text: If you knew what I knew, you wouldn't be so complacent.
We should acknowledge that things have improved, but we shouldn't be complacent.

definitions.text: The act of scouting or exploring (especially military or medical) to gain information.

examples.text: The mercenaries spied a military aircraft conducting aerial reconnaissance over the area.
We were here on a reconnaissance mission.

definitions.text: The act of wandering; deviation from truth, moral rectitude; abnormal; divergence from the straight, correct, proper, normal, or from the natural state.
A small periodical change of position in the stars and other heavenly bodies, due to the combined effect of the motion of light and the motion of the observer.

examples.text: Owing to a strange mental aberration, Tom forgot his own name.
Such a sanction is an inconceivable aberration in the application of international law.

definitions.text: To feed (a baby) milk via the breasts; to suckle; to nurse.
(chiefly of a baby) To nurse, to suck milk from a breast.

examples.text: She is embarrassed to breastfeed in public.
All moms should breastfeed their children.

definitions.text: Wearing nothing on the feet.
Transmitting without the use of an amplifier.
Wearing nothing on the feet.

examples.text: I once saw a man walk barefoot over hot coals.
Nothing hurts worse than stepping on a Lego while barefoot.
